discovery: High-resolution resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and its use to reveal spin excitations and charge order in high-temperature superconductors

nominees.name: Bernhard Keimer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research, Stuttgart, Germany

subfield: Experimental condensed matter physics / X-ray spectroscopy of quantum materials
motivation: Braicovich and Ghiringhelli turned resonant inelastic soft X-ray scattering from a coarse curiosity into a precise, momentum-resolved probe of elementary excitations, designing spectrometers (AXES, SAXES, ERIXS) that improved energy resolution by more than an order of magnitude. This made it possible to map single magnons and, with Keimer, to discover intense paramagnons persisting deep into the overdoped, superconducting cuprates, constraining spin-fluctuation pairing theories. Together they discovered incommensurate charge-density-wave order competing with superconductivity in YBa2Cu3O6+x (2012), establishing charge order as a universal feature of the cuprate phase diagram. RIXS now runs at every major synchrotron and X-ray free-electron laser, measuring spin, orbital, charge and lattice dynamics in iridates, nickelates and other quantum materials that neutrons cannot reach. Their work created a genuinely new way of seeing collective electron behaviour and reshaped how we study correlated matter.
